title: Access-Controlled Storage

Most app state is **public**: any member who reaches the app can write it.
When you need narrower rules (*only the owner*, *only this group of writers*,
*write-once*, *per-user slots*) you wrap the value in an access-controlled
collection from `calimero_storage::collections`. This page covers which wrapper
to use and how its rule holds.

## Where the rule is checked

A call runs once, on the app's leader: an attested node running the app's
signed release, never code the caller supplies. The wrapper checks the
caller's account (`env::account_id()`, set by the node from the caller's
credential) when the run writes, and refuses a write the caller may not make:
the method gets the refusal as an error, and nothing is appended. The other
replicas apply the diff the leader's run wrote; they do not run it again
([The write path](/protocol/write-path/)).

So a wrapper's rule holds because the app's code is what runs, and nobody can
skip it: not a member, not the operator. Two kinds of rule are kept by the node
itself, outside the app's code:

- **Writer sets.** A `SharedStorage` writer rotation must step from the set in
  effect, and the run's account must hold `ADMIN` in it. The node checks that
  after the run and writes the new set beside the cell, in the same entry
  ([Execution](/protocol/execution/#what-the-node-checks-after-the-run)).
- **The host's key space.** Writer sets, private spaces and blob marks live
  under `\0calimero.*`, which app code can neither read nor write by raw key.

Your own method checks (`if caller != author { bail!() }`) hold for the same
reason the wrappers do. What the wrappers add is that the rule travels with the
data: a check you forget in one method is still made by the wrapper on every
write to it.

## Storage types

Every stored entity carries a `StorageType` stamp (`crates/storage/src/entities.rs`)
that says who may write it. The wrappers below are front-ends that set the
right stamp for you.

| `StorageType` | Who may write |
|---------------|---------------|
| `Public` *(default)* | Any member who reaches the app (`DEFAULT_MEMBER_MASK`: `WRITE`+`DELETE`) |
| `User { owner: AccountId, rules }` | Only `owner`'s account, within `rules`. `rules` (`EntryRules { immutable, moderators }`) are fixed at creation: an `immutable` entry refuses changed bytes and every delete, and a `moderators` writer set may also delete it |
| `Frozen` | The first writer, once: a delete is refused, and the content cannot be modified |
| `Shared { writers: BTreeMap<AccountId, OpMask> }` | Any account in `writers`, holding the operation's `OpMask` bit |
| `SharedMember { anchor }` | The writers of `anchor`: a member carries no writer set of its own, so rotating the anchor's set changes who may write the whole subtree at once |

### Operation masks

`Shared` writers are not all-or-nothing. Each writer carries an `OpMask(u8)` —
a bitset of three independent capabilities:

| Mask | Bits | Gates |
|------|------|-------|
| `OpMask::WRITE` | `0b001` | `Put` (add / update a value or entry) |
| `OpMask::DELETE` | `0b010` | `Delete` (remove a value or entry) |
| `OpMask::ADMIN` | `0b100` | **Object ownership** — `SetWriters` / writer-set rotation |
| `OpMask::FULL` | `0b111` | All three; the default a writer gets when granted without a restriction |
| `OpMask::WRITE_ONCE` | `0b1000` | The first `Put`; a second, different `Put` seals the value. What `Frozen<T>`'s one writer holds, alone; a rotation cannot grant it beside any other bit |

The check tests individual bits via `OpMask::contains`. A `Put` requires
`WRITE`; a `Delete` requires `DELETE`; rotating the writer set requires `ADMIN`.
Because `ADMIN` is separate, a plain writer with `WRITE`+`DELETE` still cannot
lock others out by rotating an object's writer set — that needs an explicit
ownership (`ADMIN`) grant.

:::tip[Make the rule part of the data]
A wrapper makes its check on every write to it, from every method. A check
written in one method guards that method only. [Securing app state, right and
wrong](/build/guides/securing-state/) lists the mistakes we found in our own
apps, each next to the shape that holds.
:::

## Decision matrix — data need → structure

| Your data need | Use | Stamp it produces |
|----------------|-----|-------------------|
| Shared by the whole app, any member writes | a plain `#[app::state]` field (`UnorderedMap`, `LwwRegister`, …) | `Public` |
| One group of writers, set can evolve over time | `SharedStorage<T>` | `Shared` / `SharedMember` |
| A single owner, transferable | `Ownable<T>` (`= PermissionedStorage<T, OwnerAcl>`) | `Shared` with a one-key writer set |
| Per-key `WRITE` / `DELETE` / `ADMIN` capabilities | `PermissionedStorage<T, ProtocolAuthorizer>` | `Shared` with per-writer `OpMask`s |
| Named roles (`"editor"`, `"moderator"`, …) over a `DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE` | `AccessControl` | role grants in a guarded map |
| One private slot per user, keyed by identity | `UserStorage<T>` | `User { owner }` per slot |
| Write-once, content-addressed, immutable | `FrozenStorage<T>` / `ContentAddressed<C>` | `Frozen` |
| Shared keyspace, each entry owned by whoever created it | `Authored<C>` (`AuthoredMap<K, V>` = `Authored<UnorderedMap<K, V>>`) | `User { owner }` per entry |
| Owned entries nobody may ever edit or delete (signed messages, votes) | `WriteOnce<C>` | `User { owner, rules: immutable }` |
| Owned entries a moderator set may also delete | `Moderated<C>` / `ModeratedOnce<C>` | `User { owner, rules: moderators }` |
| One value fixed at `init`, forever | `Frozen<T>` | `Shared` with one `WRITE_ONCE` writer |

For which to pick, and what protects a collection nested inside a guarded
entry, see [Choosing state](/build/choosing-state/).

`SharedStorage<T>` and `Ownable<T>` are both thin aliases over
`PermissionedStorage<T, A>`: they differ only in the `Authorizer` policy `A`
(`WriterSetAcl` for group-writable, `OwnerAcl` for single-owner). Ownership
transfer (`transfer_ownership`) is an **`ADMIN` rotation** of the one-key writer
set, which the node checks like any other rotation: the capability that
`UserStorage` does not offer.

## Group-writable storage in practice

From `apps/wasmer-fixtures/kv-store-with-shared-storage`. A `SharedStorage<T>` field guards
**everything inside it**: when the wrapper holds a collection, every entry
inherits the `SharedMember` stamp, so a non-writer's write to *any* entry is
refused, not just one to the wrapper.

```rust
#[app::state(emits = for<'a> Event<'a>)]
pub struct KvStore {
    // Group-writable register; initial writer is whoever installed the app.
    shared_value: SharedStorage<LwwRegister<String>>,
    // Group-writable *map*: every entry inherits the same writer set.
    shared_map: SharedStorage<UnorderedMap<String, LwwRegister<String>>>,
}

#[app::logic]
impl KvStore {
    #[app::init]
    pub fn init() -> KvStore {
        let initializer: AccountId = calimero_sdk::env::account_id().into();
        let mut writers = BTreeSet::new();
        writers.insert(initializer);
        KvStore {
            // `false` = writer set is rotatable (pass `true` to freeze it).
            shared_value: SharedStorage::new(writers.clone(), false),
            shared_map: SharedStorage::new(writers, false),
        }
    }

    // Caller must be a current writer; the SDK refuses a non-writer's write.
    pub fn set_shared(&mut self, value: String) -> app::Result<()> {
        self.shared_value.insert(LwwRegister::new(value))?;
        Ok(())
    }

    // Ask to rotate the writer set. Caller must be a current admin; rejected if frozen.
    pub fn rotate_writers(&mut self, new_writers: Vec<AccountId>) -> app::Result<()> {
        let set: BTreeSet<AccountId> = new_writers.into_iter().collect();
        self.shared_value.rotate_writers(set)?;
        Ok(())
    }
}
```

## User-owned and write-once storage

`UserStorage<T>` gives each identity its own slot keyed by `account_id()`;
`FrozenStorage<T>` is content-addressed and immutable. This is the v1 shape of
`apps/kv-store-with-user-and-frozen-storage`:

```rust
#[app::state(emits = for<'a> Event<'a>)]
pub struct KvStore {
    items: UnorderedMap<String, LwwRegister<String>>, // Public: any member writes
    user_items_simple: UserStorage<LwwRegister<String>>, // one slot per identity
    frozen_items: FrozenStorage<String>,                 // write-once, hashed key
}

#[app::logic]
impl KvStore {
    // Writes to the CURRENT user's slot (env::account_id()). Another user's
    // slot is `User { owner }`-stamped and only that owner's account may edit it.
    pub fn set_user_simple(&mut self, value: String) -> app::Result<()> {
        self.user_items_simple.insert(value.into())?;
        Ok(())
    }

    // Returns the hex SHA-256 of the value (its key). Re-adding the same content
    // deduplicates to the same hash; the value can never be modified or deleted.
    pub fn add_frozen(&mut self, value: String) -> app::Result<String> {
        let hash = self.frozen_items.insert(value)?;
        Ok(hex::encode(hash))
    }
}
```

The app itself is now on the component SDK (`calimero-app-sdk`), where both
rules live in the collection: `PerUser<T>` keys a value by the caller's account,
so a setter has no way to name anyone else's, and `Frozen<T, H>` keys a value by
the SHA-256 of its content, inserted once and never changed. The app keeps v1's
hashes by hashing v1's borsh bytes (`BorshSha256`, a `ContentHash`, computed in
the guest with `sha2`):

```rust
#[app::state(version = 1)]
pub struct KvStore {
    items: UnorderedMap<String, String>,
    user_simple: PerUser<String>,
    user_nested: UnorderedMap<(String, String), String>, // (account, key)
    frozen: Frozen<String, BorshSha256>,
}

pub fn set_user_simple(&mut self, value: String) -> app::Result<()> {
    guards::require_member()?;
    let account = self.user_simple.set(&value)?; // the caller's own; never an argument
    env::emit(Event::UserSimpleSet { account, value }, Audience::Org)?;
    Ok(())
}

pub fn add_frozen(&mut self, value: String) -> app::Result<String> {
    guards::require_member()?;
    let (hash, _fresh) = self.frozen.insert(&value)?; // the same content stores nothing
    Ok(hash)
}
```

## `AuthoredMap` vs `UserStorage`

Both attach an identity to data, but they answer different questions.

| | `AuthoredMap<K, V>` | `UserStorage<T>` |
|---|---|---|
| Keyspace | One **shared** keyspace; keys are app-chosen | One slot **per user**, keyed by `account_id()` |
| Who inserts | Anyone may insert a *new* key (stamped with their identity) | Each user writes only their own slot |
| Who updates / removes | Only the entry's recorded **author** | Only the slot owner |
| Use it when | A collaborative collection where each row has an owner (posts, listings, claims) | Per-user private data (a profile, a personal sub-store) |

## `AccessControl`: named roles

The wrappers above bind capabilities to **keys** (a
writer set, an owner, per-key `OpMask`s). `AccessControl` adds a layer of
indirection on top: capabilities bind to **named roles** (`"editor"`,
`"moderator"`, …) and accounts are granted membership in those roles — the same
shape as OpenZeppelin's role-based access control. You grant and revoke
`"editor"` once; the gate on a method asks "does this account hold `"editor"`?"
rather than naming keys directly.

There is a single admin tier — the OpenZeppelin `DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE`. **Any admin
may grant or revoke any role**; roles do not have their own per-role admin roles.
Under the hood `AccessControl` wraps **one** `SharedStorage<UnorderedMap<…>>`
(itself a `PermissionedStorage<T, WriterSetAcl>`): the admins are exactly that
storage's writer set, and each grant is an entry
(`role\0member_hex → LwwRegister<bool>`, `true` = held, `false` = revoked) in its
writer-set-guarded map. So a non-admin's grant is refused for the same reason a
non-writer's `SharedStorage` write is: the registry entries inherit the admin
writer set. `only_admin()` and `only_role()` check the same thing up front, with
a clearer error.

### The API

| Call | Signature | Who may call | Effect |
|------|-----------|--------------|--------|
| `AccessControl::new(admin)` | `(admin: AccountId) -> Self` | — | Create with `admin` as the sole initial admin |
| `AccessControl::new_admin_caller()` | `() -> Self` | — | Same, with the current executor as admin (the `init` case) |
| `grant(role, who)` | `(&mut self, role: &str, who: AccountId)` | an admin | Give `who` the role |
| `revoke(role, who)` | `(&mut self, role: &str, who: &AccountId)` | an admin | Take the role from `who` |
| `has_role(role, who)` | `(&self, role: &str, who: &AccountId) -> Result<bool>` | anyone | Whether `who` currently holds `role` |
| `only_role(role)` | `(&self, role: &str) -> Result<()>` | — | Fail-fast: the current executor must hold `role` |
| `only_admin()` | `(&self) -> Result<()>` | — | Fail-fast: the current executor must be an admin |
| `is_admin(who)` / `admins()` | `(&self, who: &AccountId) -> bool` / `(&self) -> BTreeSet<AccountId>` | anyone | Query the admin tier |
| `grant_admin(who)` / `revoke_admin(who)` | `(&mut self, who: …) -> Result<()>` | an admin | Add / remove an admin — an **authenticated writer-set rotation** (cannot remove the last admin) |

To gate a mutation on a role, call `only_role("editor")?` before the write. To
make the data itself refuse anyone else, from every method, also project the
role onto the data's writer set (below). Admin changes go through
`grant_admin` / `revoke_admin`, which rotate the backing writer set the same way
`Ownable::transfer_ownership` does.

```rust
use calimero_sdk::{app, env, AccountId};
use calimero_storage::collections::{AccessControl, LwwRegister, PermissionedStorage};

#[app::state]
pub struct Docs {
    // The installer is the sole initial admin; admins grant/revoke roles.
    roles: AccessControl,
    // The role-gated payload lives in its own writer-set-guarded wrapper.
    body: PermissionedStorage<LwwRegister<String>>,
}

#[app::logic]
impl Docs {
    #[app::init]
    pub fn init() -> Docs {
        let me: AccountId = env::account_id().into();
        Docs {
            roles: AccessControl::new(me),
            body: PermissionedStorage::new([me].into(), false),
        }
    }

    // Admin-only: grant the "editor" role (the registry inherits the admin set,
    // so a non-admin's grant is refused).
    pub fn grant_editor(&mut self, who: AccountId) -> app::Result<()> {
        self.roles.grant("editor", who)?;
        Ok(())
    }

    // Role-gated mutation: caller must hold "editor".
    pub fn edit(&mut self, value: String) -> app::Result<()> {
        self.roles.only_role("editor")?;            // the role check
        self.body.insert(LwwRegister::new(value))?; // the writer-set check
        Ok(())
    }
}
```

For the data to refuse a non-editor whatever method writes it, push the role
memberships onto its capability map with
`AccessControl::project_onto(&[("editor", OpMask::WRITE)], &mut self.body)` after
any role change. That hands every `"editor"` the `WRITE` bit on `body`. Re-run
`project_onto` after each grant or revoke: the registry write and the projection
are separate writes.

### When to reach for it

`AccessControl` is the right choice when **the same capability is shared by a set
of accounts that changes over time, and you want to manage that set by name**.
Tie it back to the decision matrix:

| You want | Reach for |
|----------|-----------|
| One owner, transferable | `Ownable<T>` (a one-key writer set) |
| A flat group of writers, no naming | `SharedStorage<T>` |
| Per-key `WRITE` / `DELETE` / `ADMIN` bits | `PermissionedStorage<T, ProtocolAuthorizer>` |
| Named roles you grant/revoke, each conferring a capability | `AccessControl` (+ `project_onto`) |

The difference from `PermissionedStorage` is the indirection: with bare
per-key masks you re-grant every account when a policy changes; with
`AccessControl` you change the `"editor"` membership once and re-project. That
indirection is worth it when several objects share one role policy, or when
membership churns; for a single object with a fixed writer set, the plain wrappers
are simpler.

### On the component SDK

`apps/components-demo` shows all three patterns (an owned cell, a writer set, a
role registry) on the component SDK (`calimero-app-sdk`). There is no merge
plane to enforce them: every write runs on the app's leader and is replicated as
a log entry, so a check in the method against `env::caller()` is the whole
boundary. Each pattern is a table and that check:

```rust
#[derive(Record)]
#[table(key = ["role", "account"])]
pub struct Grant { pub role: String, pub account: String }

pub fn grant_role(&mut self, role: String, who: String) -> app::Result<()> {
    let me = guards::require_member()?;
    if !self.admins.contains(&me)? {
        app::bail!(Error::NotAdmin); // a refused call writes nothing anywhere
    }
    self.roles.upsert(Grant { role, account: who })?;
    Ok(())
}
```

## The #1 gotcha

:::caution[An Authorizer only protects data *inside* the wrapper]
This is the mistake that produces silently-unprotected data.

An `Authorizer` (`only_owner()`, `guard()`, the whole `PermissionedStorage`
machinery) protects **only the value stored inside the wrapper**. A value in a
plain `#[app::state]` field (a bare `String`, a `u64`, an unguarded collection)
is stamped `Public`, so **any method that writes it writes it for any member.**

This method protects less than it seems:

```rust
pub fn set_secret(&mut self, value: String) -> app::Result<()> {
    self.owner_cell.only_owner()?; // checks the owner of `owner_cell`…
    self.secret = value;           // …but `secret` is a plain Public field
    Ok(())
}
```

It stops a non-owner calling *this* method. But every other method that
writes `secret` (a `reset`, a migration you add later) writes it for anyone.

**The rule:** everything an `Authorizer` is meant to protect must live *inside*
the wrapper. Put the secret in an `Ownable<String>` (or another guarded type)
and write it through that wrapper's API.
:::

## Rotation

A writer set is not stored in the cell. `rotate_writers` checks that you hold
`ADMIN` in the set you read and records the new set on the run's outcome; the
node checks it again after the run (it must step from the set in effect, and
your account must hold `ADMIN` in it) and writes it beside the cell, in the same
entry. A TEE run, an app's own run (a handler or an xcall) and a public call
cannot rotate. Your run reads the new set back at once; every later run reads it
from state. Nothing is written to the cell, so a rotation touches no stored
byte.

Members carry `SharedMember { anchor }`, so one rotation changes the writer set
for the entire subtree at once, with no per-entity re-stamping. Rotating the
anchor is how you revoke a writer's access to everything under it.

An update that restates a different writer set is not a rotation: a write to an
existing cell whose claimed `writers` differ from the set stored with it is
refused.

Runs of one app are ordered by its log, so a rotation and a write never race:
a write after the rotation's entry is checked against the new set, and one
before it against the old.

## The caller's private state

Every wrapper above narrows *who* may write a value that every caller of the
app can read. A **private** value is narrower still: only its own account's
runs read or write it. `#[app::private]` declares a struct stored in the
caller's private space (`env::private_storage_*`, under
`\0calimero.private\0 ‖ account`): part of the app's replicated state and
sealed on disk like the rest, but handed only to runs whose caller is that
account. App code cannot address another account's space, so no wrapper is
needed: each account is the one writer of its own. See
[Execution](/protocol/execution/#three-storage-spaces-in-one-state).

Annotating a struct with `#[app::private]` generates typed accessors on it:

- `private_load()` → `Result<Option<EntryRef<Self>>>` — `None` if nothing is stored yet.
- `private_load_or_default()` → `Result<EntryRef<Self>>` — loads, or seeds `Self::default()`.
- `private_load_or_init_with(f)` → `Result<EntryRef<Self>>` — loads, or seeds from a closure.

An `EntryRef` derefs to `&Self` for reads. Call `.as_mut()` to get an `EntryMut`,
which derefs to `&mut Self` and **writes back on drop** — so a read → modify → save
cycle is just "load, mutate through `as_mut()`, let it fall out of scope." This is the
`apps/private_data` pattern:

```rust
// The caller's private state: only this account's runs read or write it.
#[derive(BorshSerialize, BorshDeserialize, Default)]
#[borsh(crate = "calimero_sdk::borsh")]
#[app::private]
pub struct Secrets {
    secrets: UnorderedMap<String, String>, // structural collection: auto-private
    secrets_added: u64,                     // plain value: no CRDT in private state
}

pub fn add_secret(&mut self, game_id: String, secret: String) -> app::Result<()> {
    // Load (or seed default), then take a save-on-drop mutable view.
    let mut secrets = Secrets::private_load_or_default()?;
    let mut secrets_mut = secrets.as_mut();
    secrets_mut.secrets.insert(game_id.clone(), secret.clone())?;
    secrets_mut.secrets_added = secrets_mut.secrets_added.saturating_add(1);
    // `secrets_mut` writes the private blob back when it drops at end of scope.

    // Only the hash goes into the shared state. (The app keeps it in an
    // `AuthoredMap` under an id naming the creator, so nobody else can change
    // the hash a guess is checked against.)
    let hash_hex = hex::encode(Sha256::digest(secret.as_bytes()));
    self.games.insert(game_id, hash_hex.into())?;
    Ok(())
}
```

For a one-liner that does not need an intermediate binding, the underlying
`private_storage::EntryHandle<T>` (returned by the generated `private_handle()`)
offers `get_or_init_with(f)` and a `modify(|state| { ... })` closure that loads,
mutates, and saves in a single call.
